column1: # Rows that are the SAME READ under two ids - 19 groups, 2026-10-24.
# Found while reading the limit-pairs row by row.
# AF_WORLDBANK_COUNTRY and WORLD_WB_COUNTRY sit 21 lines apart in
# hp3b36_africa.c and are identical in every field that decides what is
# fetched and how it is keyed - category, portal, record_type, tags, mode,
# array_path, id_keys, interval, page_param, title_keys - with VERBATIM
# identical descriptions carrying the same measurement ("295 records in 113590
# bytes"). They differ in id, name and `per_page` (400 against 500). A third
# row, WORLDBANK_COUNTRY_REGISTER, reads the same ~295 countries weekly with
# the same `id_keys = "id"`.
# So the read itself was fingerprinted across all 44,112 declarative rows:
# normalised URL + array_path + id_keys + title_keys + record_type + detail_url
# + detail_key + mode + csv_delim + post_body + next_path. Two rows sharing all
# of that fetch one collection and mint ONE set of remote_keys, so the uid
# differs only by source_id - rule 4b's double storage in its most literal
# form, plus a duplicated request every cycle.
#   19 groups, 38 rows, 19 redundant registrations. All 19 groups are inside a
#   SINGLE FILE: this is a generator emitting one source twice, not two
#   sessions colliding.
# EIGHTEEN OF THE NINETEEN DIFFER BY ONE CHARACTER: a trailing `&`.
#   https://www.castaneatownshippa.gov/?feed=rss2
#   https://www.castaneatownshippa.gov/?feed=rss2&
# Every other field matches, name and name_ja included, and the generator's own
# collision handling appended `_2` to the second id - so it noticed the NAMES
# collided and concluded it had two sources rather than one source twice.
# check_dup_endpoint cannot group them: it compares host+path+QUERY TEXTUALLY,
# and `feed=rss2` is not the string `feed=rss2&`. Neither could the limit-pair
# harvest, which requires every other query parameter to match and reads a
# record-limit difference only.
# This is the `&` family again, from a new side. The 2026-10-22 decode pass
# found 1,076 rows carrying a literal `&` and removed the nine that became
# exact duplicates once decoded. These 18 are what a decode leaves BEHIND: a
# `?feed=rss2&` becomes `?feed=rss2&`, whose trailing ampersand parses to
# nothing on the wire while still distinguishing two rows to a string
# comparison. 25 rows in the tree have a bare trailing `&` in their url, across
# seven files (hp2_eu_dach, hp3b44_{uk,us}gov, hp3b47_{fr,it,wd}gov,
# hp3b48_news); 18 of them are half of a twin pair and 7 are harmless singles
# carrying the same generator artifact.
# THE ONE GROUP THAT IS NOT A TRAILING AMPERSAND is the World Bank pair above.
# REPORTED, NOT REPAIRED. Which row of a twin group survives is a per-row
# decision and this file does not make it: the surviving id is the one other
# rows and stored uids may already reference, and `tools/cleanup_stale_uids.py`
# exists because identity changes leave rows behind in an old database. For the
# World Bank trio the cadences differ (604800 against 86400 twice) and the
# declared per_page differs (300/400/500) over a collection of ~295 records
# that fits in one page of any of them, so no reading is lost by keeping any
# one of them - but that is a judgement about three rows, and the other 18 want
# the same one made explicitly.
# TWO FALSE POSITIVES THIS CHECK PRODUCED FIRST, both from a filter that
# matched too much - the mirror of the failure in
# docs/dup-endpoints-behind-a-limit-2026-10-24.tsv, where one matched too
# little:
#   * blanking the value of every paging-ish parameter merged three different
#     SPIP feeds on lanouaille.fr (`spip.php?page=backend`,
#     `?page=backendagenda`, `?page=piclens.rss`) into one group, because
#     `page` there is a CONTENT selector. A cursor is only a cursor when the
#     row declares it, so the normaliser now blanks a cursor named by the row's
#     own `page_param` and a short list of names that can mean nothing but
#     "how many" - never `page`, `p`, `start`, `offset` or `startIndex` on name
#     alone.
#   * `urlsplit` drops the fragment silently, which reported four reads of one
#     FSA workbook (`ginkou.xlsx`, `#foreign`, `#regional`, `#regional2` -
#     sheet selectors) as one source registered four times. The fragment is
#     part of the read and is in the fingerprint now.
#   * hand-written collectors are excluded entirely: a `source_def.url` there
#     is the human-facing PORTAL and not the request template, which is why
#     four autobahn.de rows all declare `verkehr.autobahn.de/o/autobahn/` while
#     each builds a different endpoint in code.
#   31 groups before those three corrections, 19 after. The corrections only
#   ever shrink the claim.
group
